title: Fail accurately when a stale Unix control socket cannot be removed
description:
## Finding

During exclusive Unix bind, a failed liveness probe is followed by best-effort `remove_file(sock)`; its result is discarded. The subsequent bind maps every `AddrInUse` to `BindOutcome::AlreadyRunning`, even though the probe just established that no listener accepted the connection.

## Evidence

In the <issue id="d64f4288-5a12-432e-b114-562213997b6f" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-153/prevent-hardened-sandboxes-from-reaching-the-privileged-local-control">THE-153</issue> candidate's `thegn-svc/src/ipc.rs::bind_exclusive_with_hardening`, the stale-socket branch ignores unlink failure. The bind branch then classifies `AddrInUse` as an already-running daemon without a second verified connection/identity check.

## Impact

A protected but undeletable stale socket, filesystem error, race, or policy denial makes `thegn daemon` exit zero as the losing racer although no daemon is live. Callers then time out or report inconsistent state; direct startup falsely reports success.

## Required design

Treat failed stale deletion as a typed startup error. If bind returns `AddrInUse`, re-probe under the authentic lock and return AlreadyRunning only after a verified live endpoint; otherwise surface the exact filesystem/bind error. Preserve endpoint identity across the decision.

## Acceptance criteria

* Permission-denied, read-only filesystem, busy mount, replacement, and generic unlink failures never return AlreadyRunning.
* AddrInUse after a failed probe triggers bounded identity-verified reconciliation.
* AlreadyRunning always implies a successful protocol/liveness check against the intended daemon.
* Direct daemon startup never exits zero with no reachable endpoint.
* Races with concurrent winner binders still elect exactly one daemon without deleting the winner.

## Dependency mapping

Blocks <issue id="d64f4288-5a12-432e-b114-562213997b6f" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-153/prevent-hardened-sandboxes-from-reaching-the-privileged-local-control">THE-153</issue>'s relocated endpoint startup. Related to <issue id="1684dbcd-f5b4-47c9-9e68-35bce6d1bb5a" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-246/authenticate-token-only-local-control-endpoints-against-socket">THE-246</issue> server authenticity and <issue id="0803f37b-90ad-41ab-a9a8-49d8c02251b0" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-294/prevent-predictable-unix-control-runtime-pre-creation-denial-of">THE-294</issue> allocation/recovery.
